title: sopuli-dba run result
description: The single JSON document emitted by `sopuli … --output json`. One document per invocation, written to stdout after the run completes. Draft — not yet implemented.

schema_version.description: Major bumps are breaking. Consumers must accept unknown properties within the same major.

diagnostics.description: Run-level messages not attributable to a single result.

error.description: Why the run as a whole failed. Distinct from `results[].error`, which is one target failing inside a run that otherwise worked: this is present when there is no per-target work to report, as when the configuration could not be read (exit 9). Absent on success.

exit_code.description: Mirrors the process exit code. See docs/design/00-principles.md P5. 2 is the one code that never appears here: it means the invocation never parsed, so there is no run to describe and stdout is empty (03-json-output.md section 6).

policy_samples.description: What `policy sample` produced: the policy as declared, and one entry per sample describing it. Offline -- no vault, no database, and nothing generated here is stored anywhere. A sample object has no value property at all, deliberately, the same way `secret_ref` has none: `--reveal` prints to a terminal for a human to read and is refused with `--output json`, so this section cannot carry a password even by mistake.

length.description: Characters, as the policy declares. The byte limit is separate -- see `limit`.

require.description: Minimum count per character class, as declared.

limit.description: The target byte limit the samples were measured against, and the encoding it was counted in. Null when none was given: §8 measures the maximum in the database character set, so a byte count without its encoding would be meaningless.

sample.description: One generated password, described rather than given.

encoded_bytes.description: Null when no byte limit was given.

counts.description: Characters per class: upper, lower, digit, special.

compliant.description: Whether the sample satisfies the policy it was drawn from. Always true for a generated sample; false would mean the generator and the validator disagree.

config_view.description: What `config show` read, and what it resolves to. Offline: no vault or database is contacted, and no secret value appears. `resolved` discriminates the two shapes, and the allOf below holds the producer to it.

sources.description: The config files that were read, in the order they were layered.

resolved.description: false: `declared` holds the file as loaded. true: `targets` and `bindings` hold what the tool would act on.

declared.description: The merged config document, as loaded and before expansion. Deliberately untyped here: it is the user's YAML, and reshaping it would answer a different question from the one it is here to answer.

targets.description: The expanded estate. Present when resolved.

target_set.description: The target_sets entry that generated it; null for an explicit target.

managed.description: Whether any application binds an account here. A declared target that nothing manages is legitimate, not an error.

bindings.description: One row per account per target, with its secret ref rendered. Present when resolved. Grouped by the document they write, `shared_secrets` is the same rows seen the other way up.

secret.description: The SecretRef as written, rendered per account and target (01-configuration.md 7). An address, never a value. The structured form is plan.units[].secret.

shared_secrets.description: The documents more than one binding lands on, from the config alone. Present when resolved, and omitted entirely when nothing is shared. `plan.shared_secrets` is the same shape narrowed to one run's work.

timestamp.description: RFC 3339, always UTC with a trailing Z.

correlation_id.description: UUID. Also set as the Oracle client identifier via DBMS_SESSION.SET_IDENTIFIER, so it lands in UNIFIED_AUDIT_TRAIL.CLIENT_ID, and written into the vault secret metadata. One id ties all three trails together.

unattended.description: True when nobody could have been prompted. Not a flag: run context is a profile (01-configuration.md §5), and a run can be unattended for other reasons, such as a closed stdin.

selection.description: The selectors as given, before resolution.

applications.description: Application entry names. Empty in a single-application config, where the binding is inline at the top level.

options.description: Effective option values that changed behaviour, each with the precedence layer it came from.

plan.description: What the run intended to do, emitted identically for --dry-run and for a real run.

shared_secrets.description: The documents this run's work lands in that more than one binding shares. Same item shape as `config.shared_secrets`, narrowed to what the run touches.

lock.description: Advisory locks (00-principles.md P5, decided in issue #83). Locks live in the vault and are keyed on the store and the secret path being mutated -- not on the account and not on the target, because the mutated resource is the vault document and compare-and-set operates on exactly that. Three arrays, and which one a lock is in says whose it is: `held` is what this run took, `denied` is the one that stopped it, and `found` is what `lock status` read at paths it does not hold (issue #105). Absent on a run that neither took a lock nor went looking: `check`, `status` and every `--dry-run`.

mode.description: The guarantee available in the stores this section is about, not the mechanism. `cas` means every one of them has compare-and-set, so an acquisition carries a fence; `none` means at least one has no atomic primitive (KV v1, the file backend) and was configured `locking: advisory-only`, making the record a courtesy that catches operators minutes apart and misses two jobs in the same second. On a run that took locks that is what it took them under; on `lock status`, which takes none, it is what a lock in those stores would be worth. A consumer branches on this without knowing what KV v1 is.

held.description: One entry per lock, in acquisition order -- which is sorted and deterministic, so two runs contending on overlapping sets cannot deadlock.

items.description: Every field is required, including the two that are only interesting when something went wrong. This section is written when the run ends, by which point all six are known -- a partial entry would mean the producer did not know what it had locked, which is not a state worth being able to describe. `fence` is nullable rather than optional for the same reason: under mode `none` there is no fence, and saying so is different from not saying.

path.description: The secret path, not the lock record's own path. Where the record is written is the store's business.

fence.description: The version returned by the acquiring write, re-checked before every mutation. Null under mode `none`, where there is nothing to fence with.

released.description: Release writes a released record rather than deleting one: a delete leaves metadata behind, after which a first acquisition can never compare-and-set against version 0 again.

found.description: Lock records read at paths this run does not hold -- what `lock status` went looking for (issue #105). Separate from `held` because `held` is possessive: there `released: true` means this run let go cleanly, and here it would mean the path is free, which is one field meaning two things depending on `command`. In key order, which is the sorted order acquisition uses. A declared path with no record at it is not an entry: `found` is what was read, and how many paths were examined is `summary.total` -- the difference between the two is how many are free. Emitted empty rather than omitted, because on `lock status` an empty array is the finding.

items.description: One record, described by somebody who does not hold it. Every field is required for the reason `held[]`'s are: the entry exists because a record was read, so there is nothing about it left unknown.

path.description: The secret path, not the lock record's own path. Where the record is written is the store's business.

held.description: Whether this record stands in the way of taking the lock. Anything that is not `released` is held, including a `state` this build has never heard of -- treating an unknown state as free is the one guess that ends with two runs rotating one credential.

state.description: What the record says, as written. `held` and `released` are the two this build writes; anything else came from a newer sopuli, or from a half-written record, and is reported rather than flattened so that it stays recognisable. Not an enum, for that reason. `held` above is the verdict; this is the evidence.

expired.description: Whether the holder's claim has lapsed, allowing for a clock-skew margin. False on a released record, which is not a claim and has nothing to lapse.

version.description: The store's version of the record. Deliberately not called a fence -- a fence is a claim, and nothing here holds one -- but it is what a takeover has to compare-and-set against, and a version that moves between two surveys is a lock somebody is renewing. Null under mode `none`, where the number exists and guarantees nothing.

denied.description: The lock that stopped the run, on exit 7. The holder is reported so an operator can tell a colleague from a process that died -- which is the whole question at that moment. Never more than one: acquisition is all-or-nothing and stops at the first refusal.

reason.description: How the run lost. `held` means a held, unexpired record was read, and the holder and timestamps below describe it. `race` means the compare-and-set write itself was refused, which is another run acquiring between this run's read and its write -- there is nothing to report about the winner, because the winner's record was never read and re-reading it is a second round trip to answer a question the operator can answer by running again. This is why `holder` is optional: it is present exactly when it was read, and absent is a fact rather than a gap.

expired.description: True when the lock is past its expiry and was still not taken, which happens when `locking.break_expired` is off. Distinguishes a live holder from one to break.

then.description: A denial by a record that was read has to describe it. Optional-everywhere would let a producer emit `{vault, path}` on exit 7 and leave the operator with the one question this section exists to answer.

lock_holder.description: Who holds a lock, in the same shape this run's own actor is reported in. Every member is nullable and every one degrades on its own: a record written by another version, or half-written, still has to be reportable, because the alternative is a lock nobody can explain and nobody can break. Never a value -- a lock record carries an identity and a command, and no credential.

correlation_id.description: The holder's run, joinable to its own output and to the database audit trail.

shared_secret.description: One secret document that more than one binding lands on. Keyed on the document rather than on the ref, because the document is what a write, a compare-and-set and the advisory lock all operate on -- so `secret` carries a vault and a path and no field. Sharing is legal and often intended (01-configuration.md 7); it is emitted so that it is never invisible.

targets.description: Every target bound to this document: who receives the password. A document with one target still appears when several accounts share it.

accounts.description: Every account whose credential the config puts in this document (Q7, decided in issue #85). Present only when there is more than one, because a list of one is not a warning: it is the ordinary one-secret-per-account layout. `targets` answers who receives the password; this answers whose passwords a write to the document touches. Read from the config rather than from the store, so that it is offline and deterministic; an account present in the document but absent from the config is drift, which `creds check` reports.

secret_document.description: Addresses a whole secret document -- a store and a path, and nothing below them. Deliberately not `secret_ref`, for two reasons. It has no `field` or `pointer` because there is nothing here that addresses part of a document; and its `vault` is nullable, because this is emitted from the config, where a store may not have been named at all. `secret_ref` describes a ref *after* resolution, where the store is always known and C14 makes it required; that is a different moment, and `config.bindings[].vault` is nullable for the same reason this is.

vault.description: Null when the config names no store for it -- neither a `vault-name:` prefix, an application's `vault:`, the target's, nor `defaults.vault`.

secret_ref.description: Addresses a secret. Never carries a value.

scope.description: What the tool found when it connected — observed, not configured.

labels.description: Labels carried by the target, including the dimension values a target_set generated it from, e.g. {"target_set": "appdb", "env": "qa", "tenant": "delta"}. Consumers can group results by these without parsing target names.

privilege_model.description: How the tool is privileged on this target. "direct" = the service account holds ALTER USER (the standard model). "self" = connected as the account itself. "package" = the optional definer-rights package, not part of the standard install.

over_granted.description: Privileges the service account holds that the tool does not need, e.g. SELECT ANY DICTIONARY or DBA. Reported as a warning, never fatal.

offline_verify_available.description: True when SELECT ON SYS.USER$ is granted, enabling check --method hash and the LCOUNT lockout guard.

capabilities.description: Capability names the driver reported for this target.

lcount.description: Failed-login counter at the time of the check, when readable.

lockout_margin_hit.description: True when the tool declined to attempt a login because the account was near its lockout threshold.

changed.description: False for a no-op. Idempotent re-runs report changed=false.

code.description: Vendor code where one exists, e.g. "ORA-01017" or "SOPULI-20001".

hint.description: What the operator should do next.

target_capability.description: Set when category is "capability": the capability that was missing.
